chunks: Or like rain pouring from the sky which hides within it darkness, thunder and lightning. They thrust their fingers into their ears for safety against noise and death. But God surrounds those who believe not from all sides.

key_terms.الصَّوَاعِقِ: The thunderbolts or loud noises of the storm
key_terms.حَذَرَ: Out of fear or caution of
key_terms.صَيِّبٍ: Rain or shower from the sky

ai.seo_question: What is the metaphorical meaning of the storm in this verse regarding the disbelievers?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Al-Baqarah is often interpreted as depicting the spiritual paralysis of the disbelievers, whose hearts are clouded by doubt (zulumat) and whose fear of divine retribution renders them passive, covering their ears to avoid the truth. The imagery of lightning flashing like eyes yet leaving them blind underscores the paradox of their perception: they see the signs but fail to comprehend their meaning. This highlights the concept of *baqa'* (persistence) in their misguidance, where external signs do not lead to internal enlightenment.
